name: User
rationale: A base authenticated actor type is needed for requirements that apply to any user.
plain_english_summary: A person who can sign in to iTrust.
source_excerpt: ordinary authenticated user

name: HCP
rationale: HCP is a principal role that creates and edits patients.
plain_english_summary: A health care provider user.
source_excerpt: HCP

name: LHCP
rationale: LHCP is a distinct provider role created by administrators and designated by patients.
plain_english_summary: A licensed health care provider user.
source_excerpt: LHCP

name: LHCP__specialty
rationale: New LHCP creation requires a specialty value.
plain_english_summary: The medical specialty for a licensed health care provider.
source_excerpt: The administrator must specify the specialty for a new LHCP.

name: LHCP__hospitals
rationale: Administrators can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, so the LHCP needs a hospital set.
plain_english_summary: The hospitals where this licensed provider is assigned.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.
alternatives_considered: Model assignments as separate HospitalAssignment entities; rejected because the slice only needs selected hospitals.

name: Administrator
rationale: Administrator is a principal role with user and configuration management privileges.
plain_english_summary: An iTrust administrator.
source_excerpt: administrator

name: Patient
rationale: Patient is both a principal role and a resource in medical-record requirements.
plain_english_summary: A patient in iTrust.
source_excerpt: patient

name: Patient__mid
rationale: Patient MID is specifically mentioned as an identifier that must not be editable.
plain_english_summary: The patient's medical ID number.
source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.

name: Patient__name
rationale: Patient creation initially includes the patient's name.
plain_english_summary: The patient's name.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.

name: Patient__email
rationale: Patient creation initially includes the patient's email.
plain_english_summary: The patient's email address.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.

name: Patient__designatedProviders
rationale: Patient-specific DLHCP designations must be representable as a relationship.
plain_english_summary: The licensed providers this patient has designated as DLHCPs.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.
alternatives_considered: Model DLHCP as a separate global principal type; rejected because the spec emphasizes designation for that patient.

name: Patient__visitedProviders
rationale: The patient can view LHCPs with whom the patient has had office visits.
plain_english_summary: The licensed providers this patient has previously visited.
source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.
alternatives_considered: Derive solely from office visit records; rejected because the requirement directly names the viewed provider list.

name: PersonalRepresentative
rationale: Personal representative is a principal role allowed to view represented patients' records.
plain_english_summary: A user who can act for a patient they represent.
source_excerpt: personal representative

name: PersonalRepresentative__representedPatients
rationale: Represented-patient relationships are needed for record access decisions.
plain_english_summary: The patients this user is allowed to represent.
source_excerpt: for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Put representatives on Patient; rejected because the prose phrases access from the user's represented patients.

name: UAP
rationale: UAP users are created by LHCPs.
plain_english_summary: A user created by a licensed health care provider for UAP duties.
source_excerpt: UAP

name: EmergencyResponder
rationale: Emergency responders are administrator-created user roles.
plain_english_summary: An emergency responder user in iTrust.
source_excerpt: emergency responder

name: PublicHealthAgent
rationale: Public health agents are administrator-created user roles.
plain_english_summary: A public health agent user in iTrust.
source_excerpt: public health agent

name: Hospital
rationale: Hospitals are resources assigned to LHCPs by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A hospital to which a licensed provider can be assigned.
source_excerpt: multiple hospitals

name: Credential
rationale: Credentials contain MID, password, and security-question data used for authentication and secrecy requirements.
plain_english_summary: A user's sign-in and security-question information.
source_excerpt: credentials

name: Credential__user
rationale: Credentials must be tied to the user they authenticate.
plain_english_summary: The user these credentials belong to.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.
alternatives_considered: Store credential fields directly on User; rejected to make credential secrecy a distinct resource.

name: Credential__mid
rationale: MID is entered during login.
plain_english_summary: The medical ID used to sign in.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

name: Credential__hasPassword
rationale: The schema should represent password existence without exposing the password value.
plain_english_summary: Whether credentials include a password secret.
source_excerpt: password
alternatives_considered: Store password as String; rejected because the requirements are about entering and hiding the secret, not authorizing by its literal value.

name: Credential__hasSecurityQuestion
rationale: The schema should represent security-question existence without exposing the secret content.
plain_english_summary: Whether credentials include a security question secret.
source_excerpt: security question
alternatives_considered: Store securityQuestion as String; rejected because access-control policy should not depend on the secret content.

name: Session
rationale: A session resource is needed for login, logout, closure, inactivity, and resource-less authentication actions.
plain_english_summary: A user's authenticated iTrust session.
source_excerpt: authenticated session

name: Session__user
rationale: Sessions must be associated with the user whose authorization they carry.
plain_english_summary: The user who owns the session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: Session__isAuthenticated
rationale: Authorization depends on whether the session is authenticated.
plain_english_summary: Whether the session is currently signed in.
source_excerpt: authenticated session

name: Session__inactivityLimitExceeded
rationale: Authorization is disabled after the inactivity limit is exceeded.
plain_english_summary: Whether the session has been inactive for too long.
source_excerpt: after the inactivity limit is exceeded, all authorization is disabled
alternatives_considered: Use only lastActivityAt and a duration; rejected because Cedar policies cannot compute current elapsed time without context.

name: SystemConfiguration
rationale: The inactivity period length is a configurable system resource set by administrators.
plain_english_summary: System-wide iTrust settings.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: SystemConfiguration__inactivityPeriodLength
rationale: The configured inactivity period length is explicitly set by administrators.
plain_english_summary: How long a session may be inactive before authorization stops.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: ProviderList
rationale: Patients add providers to their provider list.
plain_english_summary: A patient's saved list of health care providers.
source_excerpt: provider list

name: ProviderList__patient
rationale: The provider list belongs to a specific patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient who owns this provider list.
source_excerpt: their provider list

name: ProviderList__providers
rationale: The provider list contains LHCP/HCP entries selected by the patient.
plain_english_summary: The providers on the patient's list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Use Set<LHCP>; rejected because the prose says LHCP/HCP.

name: AccessLog
rationale: Access logs are resources viewed by patients for a chosen period.
plain_english_summary: A record of accesses to a patient's information.
source_excerpt: access logs

name: AccessLog__patient
rationale: Access-log viewing is limited to the patient's own access log.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose information this access log describes.
source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log.

name: AccessLog__accessorName
rationale: Access-log results include the accessor name.
plain_english_summary: The name of the person who accessed the patient's information.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.

name: AccessLog__accessorRoleRelativeToPatient
rationale: Access-log results include the accessor's role relative to the patient.
plain_english_summary: How the accessor is related to the patient for this access.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.

name: AccessLog__accessTimestamp
rationale: Access-log results include the timestamp of access.
plain_english_summary: When the access happened.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.

name: AccessLog__transactionType
rationale: Access-log results include the transaction type.
plain_english_summary: The kind of access transaction recorded.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.

name: MedicalRecord
rationale: Medical records are resources viewed by patients and personal representatives.
plain_english_summary: A patient's medical record in iTrust.
source_excerpt: medical records

name: MedicalRecord__patient
rationale: Own-record and represented-patient access requires the record's patient identity.
plain_english_summary: The patient this medical record belongs to.
source_excerpt: their own records and for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Use owner; rejected because the domain noun is patient.

name: MedicalRecord__includesFamilyHistory
rationale: Family history is specifically included in viewable medical records.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record includes family history information.
source_excerpt: medical records including family history
alternatives_considered: Separate FamilyHistory entity; rejected because the slice treats it as included medical-record content.

name: MedicalRecord__hasPersonalHealthInformation
rationale: Personal health information is specifically viewable in own and represented records.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record contains personal health information.
source_excerpt: patient personal health information
alternatives_considered: Separate PersonalHealthInformation entity; rejected because the requirement is about sections of a record.

name: MedicalRecord__hasImmunizations
rationale: Immunizations are specifically viewable in own and represented records.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record contains immunization information.
source_excerpt: immunizations
alternatives_considered: Separate Immunization entity; rejected because this slice only needs record-section visibility.

name: MedicalRecord__hasOfficeVisitInformation
rationale: Office-visit information is specifically viewable in own and represented records.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record contains office-visit information.
source_excerpt: office-visit information
alternatives_considered: Separate OfficeVisit entity; rejected because this slice only needs record-section visibility.

name: DemographicInformation
rationale: Demographic information is listed as an important resource in the slice.
plain_english_summary: Patient demographic data such as identifying and contact information.
source_excerpt: demographic information

name: DemographicInformation__patient
rationale: Demographic information is patient data and must be tied to a patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient this demographic information describes.
source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format
alternatives_considered: Put all demographic fields directly on Patient; rejected because demographic information is named as an important resource.

name: createPatient
rationale: HCPs can create patients in the system.
plain_english_summary: Create a new patient account or patient record.
source_excerpt: An HCP can create a patient and enter the patient as a new user of the system.

name: editPatient
rationale: HCPs can edit patient data, while specific fields may be constrained in policy.
plain_english_summary: Edit patient information.
source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format, but the patient's MID must not be editable.

name: viewCredential
rationale: Credential viewing is explicitly denied for HCPs and must be a distinct action for policy.
plain_english_summary: View a user's credential secrets or security question information.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

name: editCredential
rationale: Credential editing is explicitly denied for HCPs and allowed as password-change request flow for users.
plain_english_summary: Edit credential information such as password or security question.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

name: createLHCP
rationale: Administrators create LHCP users.
plain_english_summary: Create a licensed health care provider user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: createEmergencyResponder
rationale: Administrators create emergency responder users.
plain_english_summary: Create an emergency responder user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: createPublicHealthAgent
rationale: Administrators create public health agent users.
plain_english_summary: Create a public health agent user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: assignLHCPToHospital
rationale: Administrators assign LHCPs to selected hospitals.
plain_english_summary: Assign a licensed provider to one or more hospitals.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

hospital.name: assignLHCPToHospital__context__hospital
hospital.rationale: The administrator chooses the hospital for the assignment.
hospital.plain_english_summary: The hospital being assigned to the provider.
hospital.source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

name: createUAP
rationale: LHCPs create UAP users.
plain_english_summary: Create a UAP user.
source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

name: login
rationale: Any user enters MID and password to gain role-based entry.
plain_english_summary: Sign in to iTrust.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

credential.name: login__context__credential
credential.rationale: Login uses a credential containing MID and password state.
credential.plain_english_summary: The credential being used to sign in.
credential.source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.

name: requestPasswordChange
rationale: Any user can request a password change.
plain_english_summary: Ask to change the user's password.
source_excerpt: Any user can request a password change.

name: logout
rationale: Authenticated sessions end when users log out.
plain_english_summary: End the current iTrust session by logging out.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: closeApplication
rationale: Authenticated sessions end when users close the application.
plain_english_summary: End the current iTrust session by closing the application.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: setInactivityPeriodLength
rationale: Administrators can configure the session inactivity period length.
plain_english_summary: Change the inactivity timeout setting.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: viewProviderHistory
rationale: Patients can view LHCPs they have visited or designated.
plain_english_summary: View the providers associated with a patient through visits or designations.
source_excerpt: A patient can view all LHCPs the patient has ever had an office visit with and all LHCPs the patient has designated.

name: addProviderToList
rationale: Patients add LHCP/HCP entries to their provider list using search criteria.
plain_english_summary: Add a health care provider to the patient's provider list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

provider.name: addProviderToList__context__provider
provider.rationale: The provider being added is selected by the patient.
provider.plain_english_summary: The provider to add to the list.
provider.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

searchName.name: addProviderToList__context__searchName
searchName.rationale: Search by name is part of the provider-add flow.
searchName.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

searchSpecialty.name: addProviderToList__context__searchSpecialty
searchSpecialty.rationale: Search by specialty is part of the provider-add flow.
searchSpecialty.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

searchZipCode.name: addProviderToList__context__searchZipCode
searchZipCode.rationale: Zip code is optionally used in provider search.
searchZipCode.plain_english_summary: An optional zip code used to narrow the search.
searchZipCode.source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

name: designateDLHCP
rationale: Patients can designate an LHCP as DLHCP for that patient.
plain_english_summary: Mark a licensed provider as this patient's designated provider.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

patient.name: designateDLHCP__context__patient
patient.rationale: The designation is patient-specific and must identify the patient whose designation is changed.
patient.plain_english_summary: The patient for whom the provider is being designated.
patient.source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: undesignateDLHCP
rationale: Patients can remove a patient-specific DLHCP designation.
plain_english_summary: Remove a licensed provider from this patient's designated providers.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

patient.name: undesignateDLHCP__context__patient
patient.rationale: The undesignation is patient-specific and must identify the patient whose designation is changed.
patient.plain_english_summary: The patient for whom the provider is being undesignated.
patient.source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: viewAccessLog
rationale: Patients can view their own access logs for a selected period.
plain_english_summary: View a patient's access log entries.
source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

beginDate.name: viewAccessLog__context__beginDate
beginDate.rationale: The patient chooses the beginning of the access-log period.
beginDate.plain_english_summary: The first date included in the access-log query.
beginDate.source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

endDate.name: viewAccessLog__context__endDate
endDate.rationale: The patient chooses the end of the access-log period.
endDate.plain_english_summary: The last date included in the access-log query.
endDate.source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log. The patient can choose a beginning and end date for the access-log period.

name: viewMedicalRecord
rationale: Patients and personal representatives may view medical records including family history and other sections.
plain_english_summary: View a patient's medical record.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history.

name: viewDemographicInformation
rationale: HCPs can edit patient data, and demographic information is identified as patient data/resource in the slice.
plain_english_summary: View or inspect patient demographic information.
source_excerpt: demographic information

name: editDemographicInformation
rationale: HCPs can edit patient data according to the data format.
plain_english_summary: Edit patient demographic information.
source_excerpt: The HCP can edit patient data according to the data format
